item.title: 500 remote evacuees to shelter in Nightcliff ahead of Tropical Cyclone Narelle | NT Independent
item.description: Roughly 500 Numbulwar residents will be evacuated to the Nightcliff High School gym starting midday today ahead of Tropical Cyclone Narelle, the NT Government said, with fences erected and security on site to allow classes to continue, as warnings continue for Territorians to prepare ahead of the system making landfall in the NT over the weekend.

item.title: Strike action: NT Government's move to block Alice Springs prison strike fails | NT Independent
item.description: UPDATED: The CLP Government's last minute move to block Alice Springs corrections officers from walking off the job for 12 hours has failed, with the Fair Work Commission ruling early Friday morning that the industrial action is legal and can proceed.

item.title: Christian group says former speaker Kezia Purick 'threatened physical assault' during missing ABC Radio segment | NT Independent
item.description: Disgraced former speaker Kezia Purick threatened to "personally knock" the Australian Christian Lobby "on the head" during a segment on ABC Radio's Mornings program Thursday that has not been uploaded online, which the Christian group's director says was a direct threat of violence against Christians in the Territory for their position on voluntary assisted dying.

item.title: Police officer allegedly assaulted
item.description: A flood evacuee at Marrara has been charged after he allegedly grabbed a police officer by the hair, dragged them along the ground, and hit them in the face on Saturday, NT Police said.

item.title: Attorney-General's claims about VAD legislation 'absurd', an 'embarrassment' for party: Marshall Perron | NT Independent
item.description: One of the most respected CLP chief ministers in the NT's history has publicly criticised the current CLP Government and Attorney-General Marie-Clare Boothby for "absurd" and inaccurate claims around how the Territory's first euthanasia laws came to be, while accusing the government of being "inept" over its handling of the current proposed legislation.

item.title: Boil water alert for Batchelor and Adelaide River | NT Independent
item.description: NT Health has ordered a boil water alert for Batchelor and Adelaide River following heavy rains and flooding from ex-Tropical Cyclone Narelle that Power and Water says has "impacted the water supply system" in the communities.

item.title: Woman found dead near bus stop | NT Independent
item.description: NT Police are investigating the death of a woman in her 50s who was found unresponsive near a bus stop on Karama Crescent Monday night.

item.title: Police Commissioner loses court bid to keep 'alleged conduct' of cops suppressed | NT Independent
item.description: NT Police Commissioner Martin Dole has lost a legal bid to keep "serious allegations" about misconduct of officers made by a former assistant commissioner secret, after ineffectively arguing their conduct was "sensitive" and that he preferred the allegations "remain confidential" before a potential settlement could be arranged.

item.title: Katherine Town Council ordered to reinstate former CEO
item.description: A Federal Court judge has ordered Katherine Town Council to reinstate its former chief executive officer Ingrid Stonhill and allow her to continue on worker's compensation leave until the conclusion of two unlawful discrimination complaints currently being investigated by the Australian Human Rights Commission.
